findings: In these runs Store PowerShell 7.7.0 ordinary Node children did not appear in the assigned Job; killing the Job stopped its PowerShell member but left the Node child alive.
Using the installed Store executable instead of its alias did not change the outcome.
Inbox Windows PowerShell 5.1 and bundled PowerShell 7.6.9 included the Node descendant and stopped it. Distribution versus version was not isolated; no universal claim about every PowerShell build.

The earlier ticking-child Registry probe showed stdout continuing after Job-empty, then the real one-second drain deadline destroyed the pipes. No ECONNRESET was observed. outputComplete=false was correct for that capture.

mainE2eCleanupCheck.query: Win32_Process where Name=node.exe; filter CommandLine containing long.cjs; compare ParentProcessId and CreationDate against recorded job identity before any termination
mainE2eCleanupCheck.note: No survivors remained at inspection time. This does not prove Job cleanup; no broad termination or stale-PID kill was attempted.

earlierTickingRawProbe.action: Verified WMI parent PID and exact node long.cjs command line, then Stop-Process this PID only

limitations: Only these local builds and commands were tested.
Root Job empty is evidence about Job members, not about descendants outside that Job.
A silent escaped child demonstrates that pipe shutdown cannot be relied on to terminate descendants.
